errors.description: The canvas extent holds where it needs to and no longer risks the half-canvas confusion, but it is at the deep end of the range. Measured on this 880x1168 render the front panel runs from the shoulder at y=75 to the hem at y=1130, and the pad-stitched cream chest piece stops at y=460, i.e. 36% of the panel height. That satisfies the written criterion - clearly above the interior pocket (pocket top at y=750) and roughly level with where a breast-pocket welt sits - but a literal top quarter would be nearer 30%.
errors.expected: canvas lower edge about one quarter of the way down from the shoulder seam to the hem, clearly above the interior pocket
errors.actual: canvas lower edge at 36% of the panel height, clearly above the interior pocket
errors.correction: raise the canvas lower edge a further few percent of panel height if regenerated; do not lower it, and never let it reach the interior pocket

errors.description: The pad-stitch rows read as neat machine-regular parallel dashes rather than the slightly irregular pitch of genuine hand pad-stitching. The drawing's hatch is reproduced faithfully in placement and density; only the hand-worked irregularity is missing.
errors.expected: hand pad-stitching with the slight irregularity of hand work
errors.actual: correct rows and density, but machine-regular in rhythm
errors.correction: vary the stitch pitch and row spacing very slightly so the pad stitching reads as hand-worked

notes: ATTEMPT 3 vs /images/blueprints/factory/83dbc62b46ef__00C3__Single_layer.jpg. Both outstanding findings are fixed. The hand pad-stitching that attempt 2 dropped is back and is now the most legible feature in the picture - ordered parallel rows of stitches covering the whole face of the cream haircloth piece, exactly matching the dashed-row hatch the drawing uses for that region - and the interior pocket is now a flat stitched rectangle flush with the panel instead of an applied patch. The canvas stops at 36% of panel height, well clear of the interior pocket, so the half-canvas substitution that failed attempt 1 is decisively gone and the three canvas siblings are now visually separable. Facing panel, facing seam, shell edge, lapel shape and armhole all match. Zero critical or major findings; retry budget spent.
